Oral surgery evaluation and care

Start with the right level of evaluation

A surgical dental concern can feel urgent or unfamiliar. Request an evaluation so the team can explain what is known, what needs to be reviewed, and which next step is safe to consider.

Oral surgery is a clinical category rather than a promise that every procedure is performed in this office. The confirmed Phase 3 catalog supports an oral surgery evaluation; exact in-office procedures and referral boundaries are confirmed during the visit.

Confirmed care paths

  • Oral surgery evaluation
  • Procedure-specific planning after examination
  • Comfort and aftercare discussion
  • Referral when the clinical scope or complexity requires it
Practice context

The local service catalog retains Oral Surgery as a direct service path while intentionally leaving procedure-level scope to clinical confirmation.

01

Who may be a candidate

Patients with a dental concern that may require a surgical evaluation or a referral may request an appointment.

02

What an online page cannot decide

The page does not publish an unconfirmed list of surgical procedures or imply specialty scope. The clinician determines the appropriate setting, provider, and next step after evaluation.

Start with clarity

Your Winter Park consultation

  1. 01

    Explain the concern, symptoms, prior advice, and comfort needs.

  2. 02

    Complete the examination and relevant diagnostic planning.

  3. 03

    Review the confirmed procedure scope, alternatives, recovery guidance, referral boundary, and next step.

Before you decide

What to expect

The team explains whether the concern can be addressed through the practice's confirmed scope or should be coordinated elsewhere. Timing and recovery depend on the actual procedure and are not promised here.

Ask about comfort, anxiety, and aftercare before scheduling a procedure. Sedation Dentistry is linked for a separate conversation; the appropriate option depends on clinical review.

Possible benefits

  • A clear place to start with a surgical dental concern
  • An explanation of in-office scope versus referral when relevant
  • Early discussion of comfort, preparation, recovery, and maintenance

Limitations & alternatives

  • The category does not mean every oral surgery procedure is offered in-office
  • The evaluation may lead to referral or another treatment path
  • Recovery and follow-up depend on the confirmed procedure

After your visit

Care, recovery & maintenance

Use the relevant section of the pre- and post-operative care hub only after the practice identifies the procedure. Follow the individualized instructions provided and call with recovery concerns.

Patient resourceReview pre- and post-operative careUse the guide as a supplement to the instructions provided by the practice.

Planning the investment

Insurance & financing questions

Coverage and payment depend on the confirmed procedure, provider, and plan. Ask the office to explain available information without assuming insurance coverage or financing approval.

Questions patients ask

Start with the questions that matter to you

Which oral surgery procedures are offered?

The practice has a confirmed Oral Surgery service path, but the exact in-office procedure scope is confirmed during evaluation rather than inferred from a generic list.

Will I be referred elsewhere?

Referral may be appropriate when the procedure, complexity, or provider scope requires it. The team explains that boundary during the evaluation.

Can I ask about sedation?

Yes. Share comfort concerns when requesting the evaluation. The team can discuss whether a separate sedation conversation is clinically appropriate.

Where do I find recovery guidance?

After the procedure is identified, the practice should provide individualized instructions. The linked care hub is a supplement, not a replacement for those instructions.
